Subject: Questions on token rounding and context billing for proposed Dedicated plan

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Before we move to procurement, finance has a couple of detailed asks to make sure the numbers map to our usage model:

1) If we send a request with a 60k-character document that ends up as ~10k input tokens and we get a 2k-token response, how does Redwood count that? Is it input+output or do you bill differently for context used for retrieval?

2) Do you round up to some minimum unit per request (e.g., 64 tokens, 1k tokens) or is it exact per token? We do a lot of small requests (many under 100 tokens) and want to ensure there are no hidden per-request minimums that will blow up the math.

3) For Dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing, how does rounding / monthly reconciliation work vs. Hosted? If we commit to a monthly token spend for a discount, how granular is invoice reconciliation?

4) Related: if we exceed the model's native context window (e.g., stitching multiple chunks), does Redwood bill only for the tokens actually processed, or do you count internal concatenation overhead?

We attached a draft MOP showing our expected monthly request profile (acme-draft-mop.xlsx). Can you call out the main delta drivers so I can present this to our FP&A?

Thanks,

Hi Marta —

Really useful questions — I captured the key points below and attached a short explainer (redwood-billing-explainer.pdf) that summarizes these rules with examples. Short answers up front:

- Billing unit: we bill on a per-token basis and measure tokens as the sum of tokens that enter the model (input/prompt) plus tokens generated by the model (output).
- Rounding/minimums: Hosted API is billed to the exact token (no per-request minimum). For Dedicated/committed plans we do monthly reconciliation and round invoiceable usage to the nearest 1,000 tokens for billing purposes (this is only for monthly invoice aggregation, not per-request enforcement).
- Context-window behavior: we bill only for tokens actually parsed/processed by the model. If you stitch chunks client-side and send multiple requests, each request's tokens are billed separately. Internal concatenation that happens server-side counts only the tokens fed into the model.

A bit more detail:
- Input+Output: Example — 10k input tokens + 2k output = 12k billed tokens. If you use retrieval and include retrieved context in the prompt, those retrieved tokens are billed as part of the input for that request.
- Rounding nuance: We operate exact-token accounting for Hosted to avoid surprising small-request users. For Dedicated customers on committed discounts, our finance team reconciles against the committed tier and invoices monthly; when we compute overage/usage discounts we round the monthly total to the nearest 1,000 tokens to simplify invoice line items. This rounding does not alter per-request behavior or model routing.
- Batching/caching: If you use our SDK with prefix/KV caching enabled, repeated prefixes that are served from cache are excluded from billed tokens for the model (we only bill for tokens that traverse the model). However, cache hits still count toward network/observability metrics in the console.

Next steps — I can:
- Share the redwood-billing-explainer.pdf (attached) with examples tailored to rows in your MOP.
- Pull in our billing ops lead to confirm the Dedicated reconciliation example you gave.
- Draft a revised committed-tier proposal with the monthly rounding and an estimated invoice schedule.

Hi all —

Confirming our standard enterprise billing mechanics (summarized):

1) Hosted API (self-serve): per-token exact accounting, billed on usage at end of billing period; no per-request minimums; no invoice-level rounding.

2) Dedicated / Committed contracts: customers commit to a monthly spend or token quantity. For billing clarity we reconcile actual usage against the committed quantity monthly. When generating invoices we present three line items: committed spend (discounted), overage (if usage > committed), and reconciliation rounding. For bookkeeping simplicity the overage/reconciliation lines are rounded to the nearest 1,000 tokens when converting to invoiceable tokens — this is strictly a reporting/invoicing convenience and does not change raw usage counters used for throttling or routing.

3) Discounts: the committed discount is applied to the committed quantity invoice line before rounding. Overage charges are billed at the agreed overage rate and are reconciled after applying any contractually specified rate caps.

4) Context and stitching: we only bill for tokens that the model processes. If you chunk client-side and issue multiple requests, each request's tokens are billed separately. Server-side helpers that perform concatenation still only count tokens actually provided to the model runtime.

5) Minimum invoiceable unit: we do NOT add a per-request minimum in Dedicated; the monthly rounding to 1,000 tokens is the only invoice-side granularity. So small, frequent requests remain viable economically under Hosted; for Dedicated customers the monthly aggregation tends to smooth that noise.

6) Caching/batch effects: runtime batching for throughput is an internal optimization and does not affect billing. Cache hits that avoid model execution are not billed for tokens.

If you'd like, I can run the numbers on the MOP you sent and produce a short illustration showing: (a) expected raw token consumption, (b) committed discounted invoice lines, and (c) reconciliation rounding impact. I expect the rounding noise to be <0.5% for the volumes you shared, but I'll confirm.

— Sergio
